dimensions.detail: The skill consistently describes one purpose: add, list, delete, and search TMS downloads through documented REST endpoints. The advertised homepage also resolves to a public GitHub directory for openclaw-skill-tms, matching the artifact identity. ([github.com](https://github.com/NikitaDmitryuk/telegram-media-server/tree/main/openclaw-skill-tms))
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The delete operation is destructive and removes queue/library state, local files, and qBittorrent entries, but that capability is plainly disclosed and tied to the stated download-management purpose. The artifacts would be safer with a mandatory target review and confirmation step before DELETE.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown and JSON documentation only; no executable scripts, binaries, package installers, or automatic startup hooks were present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Use of TMS_API_URL and TMS_API_KEY is proportionate for authenticated access to a TMS instance, and the README says the key should be stored in skill config rather than chat. The screenshots README should be fixed because it suggests showing TMS_API_KEY in listing screenshots without saying to redact it.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill itself creates no persistence or background worker. Persistent API-key and webhook configuration are user-managed, but enabling the skill can allow the agent to add or remove downloads unless the user restricts model invocation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The destructive DELETE capability is real and should be handled carefully, but it is not hidden or purpose-mismatched; it is a core TMS download-management operation described in SKILL.md and README.md.
[SQP-2] expected: The manifest advertises removing downloads everywhere. That is high-impact, but disclosed and coherent with the skill’s purpose; the missing caution language is a documentation safety gap rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The screenshots guidance can encourage accidental credential exposure by mentioning a config screenshot with TMS_API_KEY. No actual secret is included, and the main README gives safer secret-handling guidance, so this is a fix-before-publishing-docs issue rather than runtime exfiltration.
llm.guidance: Install this only for a TMS instance you control. Keep TMS_API_KEY in per-skill or agent secret configuration, never in chat or public screenshots, and redact any listing assets. Before deleting, list downloads first and confirm the exact id/title because deletion removes associated state and local files; restrict model invocation if you want only explicit user-requested actions.
llm.summary: This is an instruction-only skill for controlling a user-configured Telegram Media Server, with real but disclosed delete and API-key risks.
